Build a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube in a single self-contained file
`effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html` using Canvas 2D only (no WebGL, no external libraries).

Implement a minimal 3D pipeline: vertices, rotation matrices, perspective projection, and backface
culling. Split faces into triangles and do per-vertex lighting (Lambert), then rasterize the
triangles with color interpolation across each face (Gouraud shading). Add a moving light source,
a wireframe toggle (W), and pause (P). Display the current FPS.

Deliver the one file `effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html`.

{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a single self-contained HTML file: realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube using Canvas 2D only (no WebGL, no libs). Requirements:
- Full-window canvas; render into an ImageData buffer (Uint32Array view) at a lower internal resolution (e.g. 480x270-ish scaled to fit, or window size /2) and putImageData, then scale with drawImage to display canvas with imageSmoothing off or on.
- 3D pipeline: 8 cube vertices, 6 faces each split into 2 triangles (CCW winding viewed from outside). Rotation matrices Rx, Ry, Rz multiplied into a 3x3 matrix per frame with time-based angles. Translate cube to z=+4ish; perspective projection x' = cx + x*f/z, y' = cy - y*f/z.
- Per-vertex normals: use smooth averaged vertex normals (normalized vertex position for cube corners) so Gouraud interpolation is visible; rotate normals too.
- Lambert per-vertex lighting: intensity = ambient + diffuse*max(0, dot(N, L)) with a point light moving in a circle/Lissajous around the cube (L = normalize(lightPos - vertexPos)). Each face has a base color (different per face); vertex color = base * intensity + small white-ish light tint, clamped.
- Backface culling via screen-space signed area of triangle (skip if facing away).
- Rasterizer: scanline or bounding-box with edge functions/barycentric, interpolating r,g,b across triangle; also a z-buffer (Float32Array) for correctness. Top-left fill rule approx fine.
- Draw the light source as a small glowing projected dot (after raster, on display canvas with 2D arc) when in front, plus background gradient/clear to dark color.
- Wireframe toggle W: when on, draw triangle edges (visible triangles) with lines on display canvas (strokeStyle), optionally with shading off or overlaid — make W cycle to wireframe-only mode showing edges of visible triangles, including the diagonal.
- Pause P: stops rotation and light movement (time accumulator freezes) but keeps rendering/FPS.
- FPS display: smoothed FPS updated every ~0.5s, drawn top-left along with help text "W: wireframe  P: pause" and state indicators, triangle count drawn.
- Handle resize. requestAnimationFrame loop using delta time.
Code clean, commented, English."}
